To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) knowledge graph representations can be understood in terms of a simple model that predicts properties of the relations they represent; (2) this simple model explains the success of knowledge graph representation methods and the limitations of their performance; and (3) the model is able to make independent predictions about relations that are not represented in the data.

(1) knowledge graphs have a low rank structure; (2) this structure can be explained by the existence of identifiable types of relations between entities; (3) this low rank structure is captured by knowledge graph embeddings; (4) the relative performance of knowledge graph embedding models can be explained in terms of their ability to make independent, relation type-specific predictions; (5) the ability to make independent type-specific predictions is a function of the number of identifiable relation types.

(i) knowledge graph representations are interpretable, (ii) they are based on an explicit latent structure, (iii) the structure is interpretable, and (iv) it explains the relative performance of existing methods
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how knowledge graphs are represented, and the implications this has for link prediction.
understanding how knowledge graphs are represented in order to improve link prediction performance.
the following questions: (a) How do knowledge graphs relate to other data types, such as text? (b) What is the latent structure of knowledge graph data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the latent space structure of knowledge graphs, and hence their embeddings, is a function of the relational structure and not the data.
there is no single best knowledge graph representation, and the best representation is highly dependent on the application at hand.
knowledge graphs are not a good representation of knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for understanding the latent structure of knowledge graph representation models.
the structure of knowledge graphs can be represented by the structure of their representations.
we have provided a theoretical foundation for understanding knowledge graph representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge graph representation methods are not as general as often claimed, but rather they are tailored to specific tasks and knowledge graph datasets.
the latent structure of knowledge graph embeddings is not random but is determined by the underlying data.
the success of knowledge graph representation methods is due to their ability to capture latent semantic structure, which is not only interpretable but also predictive of their performance.
